---
title: "Relations among events"
---

The [event operations](events.qmd#intersection-union-and-complement) define
overlap by intersection, while the [empirical measure](probability-measures.qmd#the-empirical-measure)
assigns mass by normalized row count. Whether event probabilities can be added
directly depends on that overlap. Two events may be [**mutually exclusive**](https://bruno.nicenboim.me/bayescogsci/ch-intro.html),
**exhaustive**, both, or neither.

We classify the token events by exclusivity and exhaustivity, derive the addition rule for overlapping events, and then show why both classifications depend on the declared outcome space.

Mutual exclusivity concerns whether two events can occur together. It should not
be confused with **independence**, the later condition that learning one event
does not change the probability of the other; the
[independence page](independence.qmd) will derive that distinction.

```{r}
#| label: load-event-relations-data
library(ggplot2)

wh <- read.csv(
  "data/ud-turkish-boun/question-core-arguments.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  fileEncoding = "UTF-8"
)

stopifnot(nrow(wh) == 167L)

N_total <- nrow(wh)
p <- function(condition) mean(condition)
```

## Mutually exclusive and exhaustive events

Events $B$ and $C$ are mutually exclusive exactly when

$$
B\cap C=\varnothing.
$$

They are exhaustive exactly when

$$
B\cup C=\Omega.
$$

Within this extract, the `nsubj` event $S$ and the `obj` event $O$ are mutually exclusive and exhaustive because every retained token has exactly one of those two source relations. Countable additivity thus gives

$$
\mathbb{P}(S\cup O)
=
\mathbb{P}(S)+\mathbb{P}(O)
=1.
$$

```{r}
#| label: compute-exclusive-events
p_subject <- p(wh$dependency_relation == "nsubj")
p_object <- p(wh$dependency_relation == "obj")
p_both_relations <- p(
  wh$dependency_relation == "nsubj" &
    wh$dependency_relation == "obj"
)

stopifnot(
  p_both_relations == 0,
  isTRUE(all.equal(p_subject + p_object, 1))
)

c(subject = p_subject, object = p_object,
  intersection = p_both_relations)
```

Mutual exclusivity does not imply exhaustivity. The *hangi* and *kim* lemma events share no token, but their union excludes the *ne* tokens observed in the same extract.

| Structural question | Set condition | Probability consequence |
|---|---|---|
| Mutually exclusive? | $B\cap C=\varnothing$ | no overlap term is needed |
| Exhaustive? | $B\cup C=\Omega$ | the union has probability one |
| Both? | $C=B^c$ | $\mathbb{P}(B)+\mathbb{P}(C)=1$ | <!-- dqr-allow: symbolic-derivation -->
| Neither? | overlap and omission both remain | use the full union formula |

## Overlapping events

The *ne* event $N$ and object event $O$ overlap. For arbitrary events,

$$
\mathbb{P}(B\cup C)
=
\mathbb{P}(B)+\mathbb{P}(C)-\mathbb{P}(B\cap C).
$$

The subtracted term repairs the double count of outcomes in the intersection.

```{r}
#| label: compute-overlapping-events
is_ne <- wh$lemma == "ne"
is_object <- wh$dependency_relation == "obj"

p_ne <- p(is_ne)
p_object <- p(is_object)
p_intersection <- p(is_ne & is_object)
p_union_direct <- p(is_ne | is_object)
p_union_formula <- p_ne + p_object - p_intersection

stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(p_union_direct, p_union_formula)))

c(ne = p_ne, object = p_object,
  intersection = p_intersection,
  union = p_union_direct)
```

The intersection has empirical probability `r round(p_intersection, 3)`. Thus adding the two marginal probabilities without subtracting the intersection would exceed the probability of their union by exactly that amount.

```{r}
#| label: plot-event-relations
#| fig-cap: "Empirical masses in the four disjoint cells formed by the *ne* and object events."
cells <- as.data.frame(xtabs(~ ne_lemma + object, data = wh))
names(cells)[3] <- "tokens"
cells$probability <- cells$tokens / N_total
cells$lemma_event <- ifelse(cells$ne_lemma == 1, "ne", "other lemma")
cells$relation_event <- ifelse(cells$object == 1, "obj", "nsubj")

ggplot(cells,
       aes(lemma_event, probability, fill = relation_event)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", color = "white") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(nsubj = "grey", obj = "steelblue")) +
  labs(x = "Lemma event", y = "Empirical probability",
       fill = "UD relation") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)
```

## Dependence on the outcome representation

Mutual exclusivity is relative to what one outcome represents. If one outcome is one retained token, the two relation labels are mutually exclusive. If one outcome were a sentence, the events “the sentence contains an `nsubj` interrogative token” and “the sentence contains an `obj` interrogative token” could co-occur. Changing the unit changes the event relation.

Labels alone do not guarantee mutual exclusivity. The *ne* event is a lemma property, whereas the object event is a syntactic-relation property, so one token may belong to both. The source's annotation schema tells us whether the coded values can co-occur.

Additivity without an overlap correction is licensed by disjointness, not by the familiarity of the labels. The [next page](joint-probability-of-events.qmd) records every intersection in one table.

## Check your understanding

1. Compute the probability of the union of the *hangi* and *kim* events. Why is no intersection subtraction needed?
2. Verify the union formula for the *kim* and `obj` events.
3. Are the three lemma events exhaustive in the extract? Use code rather than the README count.
4. Describe a sentence-level outcome representation under which `nsubj` and `obj` interrogative events could co-occur.
5. A student says that the mutually exclusive lemma events *hangi* and *kim*
   must be independent. What does their empty intersection imply instead?

<details class="understanding-answers">
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. $\mathbb{P}(H\cup K)=20/167=0.119760$; no intersection term is needed because a token cannot have both the *hangi* and *kim* lemmas. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
2. $\mathbb{P}(K\cup O)=17/167+116/167-3/167=130/167=0.778443$. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
3. Yes; the counts for *hangi*, *kim*, and *ne* are $3+17+147=167$, exactly the number of retained rows. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
4. With one sentence as an outcome, the `nsubj` event and `obj` event could co-occur when that sentence contains one interrogative subject token and another interrogative object token. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
5. Their joint probability is zero. Since both marginal probabilities are
   positive, their product is positive, so they are not independent.

</details>

Exclusivity and exhaustivity make different set-theoretic claims: the former
requires an empty intersection, while the latter requires a union equal to
$\Omega$. When events overlap, their joint mass must be subtracted once. The
[next page](joint-probability-of-events.qmd) records all four intersections and
their margins in one table.
